name: rasterize_clipped_edge_pair
description: Steps two fixed-point edges in lockstep and calls a per-row handler through an indexed jump table only for rows whose column stays below 321. A width comparison selects between two loop bodies, and a sign test decides which edge is advanced first.

name: step_edge_pair_rows
description: Advances two edges one row at a time with fixed-point increments, deriving a slope quotient from the second parameter pair. The row handler is called through a table for in-range columns, and the routine returns after both edge loops finish.

name: step_fixed_point_edge_rows
description: Accumulates fixed-point steps for one edge and calls the row handler through a jump table for each in-range row. A sign test swaps the accumulators before a second pass over the remaining rows.

name: walk_fixed_point_span
description: Steps a fixed-point accumulator across a span of columns and calls the per-column handler through a jump table whenever the column is below 321. The loop counts down from the span length to minus one.

name: step_span_with_accumulators
description: Steps a pair of accumulators across a span and calls the per-column handler through a table when the column is in range. A sign test selects which accumulator carries forward into the loop.

name: draw_span_counting_down
description: Counts a row index down from its start value to minus one, advancing two accumulators and calling the handler through a table when the column is below 321. The only bound check is that column test.

name: rasterize_edge_pair_by_slope
description: Derives a slope from the parameter pair by division, then steps two edges row by row and calls the handler through a jump table for in-range columns. A sign comparison decides which accumulator advances first.

name: step_edge_rows_by_division
description: Divides a horizontal difference by a vertical difference to obtain a fixed-point slope, then steps the edge rows and calls the handler through a jump table for in-range columns.

name: emit_pixels_along_span
description: Advances two accumulators across a span whose length comes from a register value, calling the handler through a table for each column below 321. The routine has no division and no second edge.

name: walk_span_rows_bounded
description: Steps two accumulators through a row count and calls the handler through a jump table when the position stays below 321. It applies a single fixed-point increment per row rather than a slope division.

name: walk_span_columns_reverse
description: Counts a row count down while stepping two accumulators, calling the handler through a table for in-range positions. The accumulators are used in the opposite order from the forward span walker.

name: clip_edge_pair_by_height
description: Clips a pair of edge segments against a vertical range, dividing coordinate differences to get slopes and calling the handler through a jump table for in-range rows. Sign comparisons choose which edge supplies each starting position.

name: clip_edge_pair_then_rasterize
description: Computes slopes for two edges by division, then runs row loops that call the handler through a jump table for in-range positions. Separate branches handle clipped and unclipped segments.

name: step_clipped_edge_by_width
description: Steps two edges against a width limit, choosing the loop order from a comparison of the two horizontal extents. The handler is called through a table for in-range columns.

name: rasterize_edge_pair_clipped_width
description: Steps a pair of edges across a span limited by width, with the second edge's slope computed by division. The handler is called through a jump table for in-range columns.

name: step_left_right_edge_rows
description: Steps a left and a right edge row by row with fixed-point increments, using a division to derive one edge slope. The handler is called through a table for in-range columns.

name: walk_column_span_handler
description: Steps two accumulators across a count of columns and calls the handler through a jump table when the column is below 321. Only a single countdown loop is present.

name: step_span_accumulators_forward
description: Steps two accumulators forward across a row count and calls the handler through a jump table for in-range columns. A sign flag selects which accumulator is advanced.

name: count_down_span_handler_calls
description: Counts a row value down from its start to minus one, advancing two accumulators and calling the handler through a table for columns below 321. It has no clipping branch beyond that bound check.

name: rasterize_slope_edge_pair
description: Derives slopes for two edges from the parameter pair by division, steps both edges row by row, and calls the handler through a jump table for in-range columns.

name: step_edge_pair_by_quotient
description: Steps two edges row by row with fixed-point increments, deriving one edge's slope from a quotient of the parameter differences. The row handler is called through a jump table for in-range columns.

name: walk_span_column_positions
description: Walks a span of columns from its start, advancing two accumulators and calling the handler through a table for each position below 321. The loop runs until the counter reaches minus one.

name: step_pair_of_accumulators
description: Advances a pair of fixed-point accumulators across a row count and calls the handler through a table for in-range columns. A sign flag decides which accumulator is updated first.

name: draw_rows_countdown_accumulators
description: Counts a row value down to minus one while advancing two accumulators, calling the handler through a table for columns below 321. Each step applies one fixed-point increment without any division.

name: dispatch_indexed_handlers_bounded
description: Checks that two coordinates lie between 2 and 317 and between 2 and 165, then calls up to five table handlers in a sequence chosen by a count argument. Out-of-range coordinates return without any call.

name: call_two_fixed_offset_handlers
description: Invokes two handlers in sequence, each looked up at a fixed offset from a table block held in a register. No index is computed and no loop is involved.

name: invoke_mixed_table_handlers
description: Calls three handlers in sequence, two through fixed offsets of a table block and one through a pointer read from memory. No loop or arithmetic appears.

name: call_three_fixed_offset_handlers
description: Calls three handlers in sequence, each looked up at a fixed offset from a table block passed in a register. The routine has no branches.

name: call_four_table_handlers
description: Calls four handlers in sequence, two at one fixed table offset and two at another. The routine has no branches and no arithmetic.

name: return_without_work
description: This is an empty routine that returns immediately without executing any further instructions.

name: build_edge_table_then_fill
description: For counts below six it calls up to five table handlers in a fixed sequence. For larger counts it builds a stack table of edge positions and then walks it, calling the handler for each in-range column.

name: fill_edge_table_rows
description: Writes pairs of values into two stack cursors for each row between two bounds while stepping an edge. It then calls the handler through a table for each in-range column of the row.

name: dispatch_word_pairs_to_handler
description: Iterates over a list of word pairs, adds each pair's values, and applies sign and range checks to the sum. For in-range results it calls the handler through a table indexed by the computed value.

name: emit_edge_table_rows
description: Writes a value pair for each row of an edge table and then calls the handler through a table for each in-range column. A comparison selects the branch that finishes the last row.

name: walk_line_by_major_axis
description: Chooses the longer of the horizontal or vertical extents as the stepping axis and accumulates a minor-axis error term. It calls the per-pixel handler through a table at each step and returns the handler's last result, or minus one when the count is exhausted.

name: step_line_pixels_with_error
description: Steps along the major axis of a line using an error accumulator and calls the per-pixel handler through a table for each step. It returns the handler's final result, or minus one if the step count runs out.

name: step_line_overflow_handler
description: Steps an error accumulator through a count of columns and calls the handler through a table whenever the accumulated value overflows. It makes one final handler call at the end of the count.

name: count_down_line_steps
description: Counts a step value down while accumulating a fixed-point error term, calling the handler through a table at each step. The loop ends when the count is used up or the accumulator wraps around.

name: walk_line_all_octants
description: Selects one of several octant cases from the signs and magnitudes of two deltas, then steps the line and calls the handler through a table for each step. It covers both orientations of the major axis.

name: advance_line_error_draw_pass
description: Advances an error accumulator through a count of columns and calls the handler through a table whenever the value overflows. Its loop structure matches the other overflow-step line walkers in this group.

name: step_line_countdown_handler
description: Counts a step value down while accumulating a fixed-point error term, calling the handler through a table at each step. A negative count returns immediately, and otherwise the last handler result is returned.

name: walk_line_mirrored_octants
description: Steps a line by one of several octant cases chosen from the signs and sizes of two deltas, calling the handler through a table at each step. Each case returns the handler's last result, or minus one when the count is used up.

name: walk_line_error_overflow_calls
description: Steps an error accumulator through a count of columns and calls the handler through a table on each overflow. It makes one further call when the count ends.

name: count_line_steps_return_last
description: Steps a count down while accumulating an error term and calls the handler through a table at each step. A negative count returns at once, and the handler's result is returned when the loop finishes.

name: step_line_across_octants
description: Branches on the signs of two deltas into one of several octant loops, calling the handler through a table at each step. Only some branches contain the error-term overflow step.

name: emit_line_overflow_handler_calls
description: Steps an error accumulator through a count of columns and calls the handler through a table whenever the value overflows. A final handler call is made after the count is exhausted.

name: count_line_steps_down_table
description: Counts a step value down while accumulating an error term and calls the handler through a table at each step. A negative count returns at once.

name: draw_clipped_segment_points
description: Steps two pairs of fixed-point coordinates for a counted number of points and tests each position against a 320 by 168 screen area. It calls a point-drawing routine for each position, with a different number of calls depending on whether the point lies inside the area.

name: walk_stacked_points_clipped
description: Takes its coordinates and counter from stacked arguments, steps two coordinate pairs, and calls a point-drawing routine for positions inside the 320 by 168 area. It exits when the counter goes negative.

name: emit_clipped_point_run
description: Calls a point-drawing routine twice at the start of each pass, then steps coordinates and emits further points while they stay inside the 320 by 168 area. A stacked counter limits the number of passes.

name: return_immediately_empty
description: This routine has no body beyond a return and executes no instructions.

name: call_handler_four_times
description: Calls the same handler four times in a row and then returns, with no other operations in between.

name: blit_sprite_rows_bitplanes
description: Clips a sprite against a 320 by 168 window, then either shifts and masks its words into a single bitplane when the left edge is not 16-aligned, or copies its words across four bitplanes when it is aligned. Some cases call a table handler per row instead.

name: blit_sprite_tall_window
description: Performs the same sprite clipping and bitplane copy as the 168-row variant, but the window allows rows up to 200. Unaligned sprites are shifted into one plane and aligned sprites are copied across four.

name: copy_block_across_bitplanes
description: Copies blocks of ten words from a source into four bitplanes using separate copy loops for each plane. It calls a table handler per cell when a selector value is not 18 and the zero flag is clear.

name: fill_grid_or_copy_planes
description: Calls a table handler for each cell of a grid when a selector value is not 18, and otherwise copies blocks of ten words into four bitplanes. The handler path and the copy path are separate loops.

name: execute_function_loop
description: Looks up a function pointer in a table using an offset and calls it in four nested count-down loops, each with its own counter.

name: copy_long_word_pair
description: Copies one 32-bit value and one following 16-bit value from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_two_longs
description: Copies two consecutive 32-bit values from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_five_words
description: Copies five consecutive 16-bit values from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_three_longs
description: Copies three consecutive 32-bit values from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_seven_words
description: Copies seven consecutive 16-bit values from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_four_longs
description: Copies four consecutive 32-bit values from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_eight_words
description: Copies eight consecutive 16-bit values from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_five_longs
description: Copies five consecutive 32-bit values from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_five_longs_and_word
description: Copies five 32-bit values followed by one 16-bit value from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_six_longs
description: Copies six consecutive 32-bit values from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_six_longs_and_word
description: Copies six 32-bit values followed by one 16-bit value from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_seven_longs
description: Copies seven consecutive 32-bit values from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_seven_longs_and_word
description: Copies seven 32-bit values followed by one 16-bit value from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_eight_longs
description: Copies eight consecutive 32-bit values from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_eight_longs_and_word
description: Copies eight 32-bit values followed by one 16-bit value from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_nine_longs
description: Copies nine consecutive 32-bit values from a source block to a destination block.

name: copy_nine_longs_and_word
description: Copies nine 32-bit values followed by one 16-bit value from a source block to a destination block.

name: merge_shifted_word_column
description: When the width is one block, it calls a handler three times and then merges a shifted source word into one bitplane column for each row. The merge clears the existing bits with a mask before OR-ing in the new value, stepping 40 bytes per row. Otherwise it calls a handler four times and returns.

name: merge_shifted_words_by_count
description: Loops a counted number of times, combining each destination long with a source word that is shifted by a register amount. The source advances by one word and the destination by 40 bytes per iteration.

name: invoke_routine_four_times
description: Calls one routine four times in succession and then returns.

name: shift_and_mask_word_array
description: Walks a two-dimensional array of words row by row, shifting each value left by a register amount and combining it with the destination through a mask. Row and column counts come from registers.

name: return_without_action
description: This routine consists of a single return and performs no action.

name: return_with_no_effect
description: The routine returns directly to its caller without executing any other operation.

name: shift_input_left_five
description: Shifts the 16-bit input value left by five bits and returns the result.

name: xor_word_at_offset
description: Computes a word address from a base register, a doubled index, and a fixed offset, then XORs a second register value into the word at that address.

name: dispatch_band_rows_two_handlers
description: Calls a table handler once per row of a band for a counted number of rows, switching to a second handler when a counter derived from the input coordinate minus 167 reaches a boundary. It returns early when a stacked flag is set.

name: invoke_two_routines_in_order
description: Calls two routines in order and then returns, with no other operations.

name: draw_run_with_table_handler
description: Checks that a start coordinate plus a width stays below 198, reducing the width if it overflows, and then calls a table handler once per unit of the count. When the low four bits of the first argument are zero it makes an extra call to a second routine first.

name: call_table_handler_countdown
description: Calls a handler at a fixed table offset once per pass of a loop that runs until its counter reaches minus one.

name: scale_products_into_range
description: Forms two products from the inputs, halves them together until the first lies within plus or minus 7935, then halves the second on its own to the same range. It returns the adjusted first product.

name: halve_pair_into_range
description: Halves the first value until it is at most 7935, halving the second value alongside it, then halves the second value alone until its magnitude is within 7935.

name: halve_value_into_range
description: Halves a signed 16-bit value repeatedly until its magnitude is at most 7935.

name: halve_while_above_limit
description: Halves a positive 16-bit value repeatedly while it exceeds 7935, leaving negative values unchanged.

name: exit_with_no_work
description: This routine consists of a single return and does nothing else.

name: multiply_pair_then_halve
description: Multiplies two inputs by a third value, keeping the high part of each product, then halves the pair until the first lies within plus or minus 7935 and brings the second into the same range. It returns both values as one 32-bit result.

name: halve_pair_into_range
description: Halves the first value until it is at most 7935, halving the second value alongside it, then halves the second value alone until its magnitude is within 7935.

name: halve_value_into_range
description: Halves a signed 16-bit value repeatedly until its magnitude is at most 7935.

name: halve_while_above_limit
description: Halves a positive 16-bit value repeatedly while it exceeds 7935, leaving negative values unchanged.

name: return_without_effect
description: The routine returns directly to its caller without changing any value.

name: normalize_multiply_pair_table
description: Shifts a set of inputs right until they fit 16 bits, then scales a pair of values by table entries chosen by the magnitude of a third value. Three magnitude ranges select different lookups and halving loops, and both scaled values are returned in one packed result.

name: shift_negative_then_scale_pair
description: Shifts the first input right while it is below minus 32768, applying the same shifts to the paired values. It then scales the pair by a table entry chosen by magnitude, with the same three ranges and halving loops, and returns a packed result.

name: scale_pair_when_within_bounds
description: Shifts the paired values right when the second input lies within the magnitude of the third, then scales the result by a table entry chosen by magnitude. The shift is gated on that range check, which the other pair scalers do not apply.

name: scale_pair_by_magnitude_table
description: Shifts the second input right while it is below minus 32768, then scales the pair using a table lookup chosen by magnitude. Small magnitudes use one lookup and larger ones use a shifted index, and a packed pair is returned.

name: normalize_abs_scale_pair
description: Compares the magnitudes of the inputs and shifts the pair right until they fit 16 bits. It then scales the pair by table entries chosen by magnitude over three ranges, and returns a packed result.

name: scale_pair_table_then_halve
description: Multiplies both inputs by a table entry chosen from the third input, keeping the high part of each product, then halves the pair into the plus or minus 7935 range. Only the first scaled value is returned.

name: scale_pair_by_table_entry
description: Multiplies both inputs by a table entry selected from the high bits of the third input and returns the two products packed together, with no range adjustment.

name: halve_fit_then_table_scale
description: Halves both inputs together with the third value until the third fits in 16 bits, then multiplies the pair by a table entry chosen from the reduced third value. Both products are returned packed together.

name: offset_helper_result_or_min
description: If the count argument exceeds 63 it calls a helper, adds 160 to its 16-bit result and returns that. Otherwise it returns minus 32768.

name: return_minimum_short_value
description: Returns the 16-bit constant 32768, which is the bit pattern of the most negative signed 16-bit value.

name: compute_vector_length_ratio
description: Takes absolute values of three components, sums their squares with fixed-point multiplies, and finds the square root bit by bit. It then divides a component by that root and returns the ratio multiplied by a further register value.

name: scale_quotient_by_sqrt
description: Computes an integer square root of a fixed-point value by bit-wise iteration, then divides two components by that root in the same way. It returns the third quotient scaled by a fourth value.

name: find_leading_bit_value
description: Calls a helper for a 16-bit value, halves it, and doubles a running value until its sign bit is set. It returns the last value below that bit, masked to 15 bits, or zero when the halved value is zero.

name: halve_helper_result
description: Calls a helper to obtain a 16-bit value and returns that value shifted right by one bit.

name: lookup_squared_length_scale
description: Sums the squares of three 16-bit inputs, then shifts the sum into one of three size ranges and looks up a table entry for the reduced value. The entry is returned shifted by an amount that depends on the range.

name: lookup_value_range_scale
description: Looks up a scaled table entry for a 32-bit input, choosing among shift-and-lookup paths by the input's size, including a top range. The entry is returned shifted by the path's amount.

name: lookup_table_halved
description: Uses the input shifted right by two as a table index and returns the table entry shifted right by one.

name: fetch_table_entry_index_shift
description: Returns a 16-bit table entry at an index formed by shifting the input right by four bits.

name: lookup_range_scale_wide
description: Looks up a table entry for a 32-bit input, choosing among three shift-and-lookup ranges by size, and returns the entry shifted by the range's amount.

name: lookup_scaled_high_range
description: Swaps the halves of a 32-bit input, shifts it left by two, and uses the result as a table index. The entry is returned shifted right by three.

name: lookup_scaled_mid_range
description: Swaps the halves of a 32-bit input, shifts it left by six, and uses the result as a table index. The entry is returned shifted right by five.

name: compute_dot_product_pair
description: Computes two dot products between a three-component vector held in registers and the first and second columns of a 3 by 3 table in memory, doubling each sum. Both results are returned packed into one 64-bit value.

name: compute_matrix_row_dot_pair
description: Computes dot products between a three-component register vector and the first two rows of a 3 by 3 table in memory, doubling each sum. Both results are returned packed together in one 64-bit value.

name: build_rotation_matrix_from_angles
description: Looks up table values for two angle inputs, applying sign flips from the top bit of each angle, and writes nine 16-bit entries into an output block. The eighth entry of the block is set to zero.

name: build_matrix_stacked_angles
description: Builds a nine-entry 3 by 3 matrix from table values for angles passed on the stack and in a register, applying sign flips from each angle's top bit. One entry of the block is set to zero.

name: build_matrix_mixed_inputs
description: Writes a nine-entry matrix using table values for angles from a register and from the stack, with one input stored directly. One entry of the block is set to zero.

name: build_matrix_direct_values
description: Writes a nine-entry matrix in which two inputs are stored directly and the other two come from table values with sign flips. One entry of the block is set to zero.

name: build_rotation_matrix
description: Writes a nine-entry matrix from one table value and three direct register inputs, with one entry set to zero. The table value is read at an index taken from a register.

name: build_matrix_two_angles_signed
description: Looks up table values for two register angles, applies sign flips from each top bit, and writes a nine-entry matrix with one entry set to zero.

name: build_matrix_two_stacked_angles
description: Writes a nine-entry matrix from table values for two stacked angles and one register angle, applying sign flips. One entry of the block is set to zero.

name: build_matrix_stacked_and_direct
description: Writes a nine-entry matrix using table values for two stacked angles and a directly supplied register value. One entry of the block is set to zero.

name: build_negated_matrix_entries
description: Writes a nine-entry matrix from two table values and two direct inputs in a transposed layout, with several entries negated. One entry of the block is set to zero.

name: build_transposed_matrix_direct
description: Writes a nine-entry matrix in a transposed layout using one table value and three direct inputs, with several entries negated. One entry of the block is set to zero.

name: compute_table_product_pair
description: Looks up table values for two angle inputs, with a quarter-turn offset for one of them, applies sign flips, and returns two products packed into one 64-bit result.

name: compute_signed_table_product_pair
description: Looks up signed table values for two register inputs, multiplies one table value by the first input, and returns two products packed into a 64-bit result.

name: compute_direct_table_product_pair
description: Multiplies a register input by a table value, multiplies two signed table values together, and returns both products packed into one 64-bit result.

name: compute_product_with_table_pair
description: Multiplies two register inputs together, multiplies the second input by a signed table value, and returns both products packed into one 64-bit result.

name: compute_product_pair_unsigned_table
description: Multiplies two register inputs and multiplies the second by a table value read without a sign flip. Both products are returned packed into one 64-bit result.

name: clip_point_to_screen_edge
description: Moves a point that lies outside the 320 by 168 screen area back along a segment, using halving steps until it reaches the edge. The adjusted coordinates are returned packed into one 64-bit value.

name: clip_point_along_segment_bounds
description: Repeatedly halves a step along a segment until the point falls inside the 168-row screen limit. The point's coordinates are returned packed into one 64-bit value.

name: converge_point_by_halving
description: Halves two step values and adjusts a point by them until the vertical step falls below 64. The point's coordinates are shifted down by eight bits and returned packed into one 64-bit value.

name: clip_point_below_screen_edge
description: Adjusts a point whose vertical coordinate exceeds 168 using halving steps along a segment, returning the adjusted coordinates packed into one 64-bit value. Points within range are returned unchanged.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler produced only a return for this body, so the 85 recorded instructions were not recovered and no behaviour can be stated from the code.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler produced only a return for this gap, so the 14 recorded instructions were not recovered and the routine is a stub or undecoded data.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler produced only a return for this body, so the 14 recorded instructions were not recovered and no behaviour can be stated from the code.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler produced only a return for this gap, so the 31 recorded instructions were not recovered and the routine is a stub or undecoded data.

name: rotate_component_pairs_by_angle
description: Rotates three pairs of 16-bit components, one value from each input block, by a cosine and sine pair taken from a table at a register angle. The rotated values are written back into both blocks.

name: rotate_component_pairs_table_index
description: Rotates three component pairs in two input blocks using table values, with one table value read from an index register and a second angle supplied in a register. The results are written back into both blocks.

name: rotate_component_pairs_direct_coeff
description: Applies a rotation to three component pairs in two blocks, using one coefficient taken directly from a register and one table value. The results are written back into both blocks.

name: insert_key_into_search_tree
description: Inserts a new node carrying a key into a binary search tree whose nodes hold a key and two child links. It moves right when the node's key is smaller and left otherwise, and sets the new node's child links to zero.

name: attach_key_to_tree_branch
description: Walks down a tree of key nodes, moving to the left child while the new key is not larger, and attaches the new node in the first empty child slot reached. The new node's child links are set to zero.

name: initialize_tree_root_node
description: Sets up a root node in a shared memory block by zeroing its key and child links and storing a fixed signed word. It then points the tree cursor globals at that node and sets several other global constants.

name: reset_tree_root_node
description: Clears a global value and re-initializes the root node the same way as the initialization routine, zeroing the key and child links and resetting the cursor globals and constants.

name: set_global_pointers_to_stack
description: Sets three global pointers to the address of a large local buffer on the stack.

name: traverse_nodes_calling_handlers
description: Traverses a linked structure of nodes depth-first, calling a handler chosen from a table by each node's stored index. It walks back up through saved links when a subtree is finished.

name: traverse_tree_from_root
description: Starts a depth-first traversal at a root node held in a global, calling a table handler for each node visited. It climbs back through saved links as each subtree completes.

name: return_immediately_empty
description: This routine consists of a single return and executes no other instructions.

name: refresh_transformed_vectors_if_stale
description: When a generation flag differs from the stored one, it multiplies a 3 by 3 matrix block by three helper vectors, stores the nine resulting components, and records the current flag. Otherwise it returns unchanged.

name: accumulate_scaled_transform_result
description: Computes a matrix-vector product from a 3 by 3 block, with the inputs shifted to fit a magnitude count. It adds the result into six 32-bit accumulators with carry propagation and then records a generation flag.

name: add_scaled_vector_to_accumulators
description: Shifts three input values to fit a magnitude count, multiplies them by a 3 by 3 table, and adds the results and the parameter values into six 32-bit accumulators with carry propagation.

name: store_shifted_accumulated_values
description: Shifts three register values right by a shared count and adds each to a parameter. It stores the sums with carry flags into six 32-bit accumulators and then records a generation flag.

name: fetch_accumulated_pair_refreshing
description: Returns the first two accumulators as a 64-bit value, first refreshing them when the stored flag differs from the current generation. A second flag selects an extra shift-and-accumulate step before the return.

name: fetch_accumulated_pair_flagged
description: Returns the first two accumulators as a 64-bit value, refreshing them when a flag in a register differs from the stored flag. Otherwise it returns the cached pair.

name: fetch_cached_accumulator_pair
description: Returns the two 32-bit accumulators stored at a fixed offset as one 64-bit value, with no refresh.

name: copy_cached_accumulators
description: Copies six 32-bit values from one fixed-offset block to another, then records the current generation flag.

name: diff_cached_accumulator_pairs
description: Returns the difference between two stored accumulator pairs when their flags match, negated when the flags indicate a reversed comparison. Otherwise it calls a helper and subtracts the stored pair from its result.

name: diff_cached_pair_or_helper
description: Compares two structures' flags and returns the difference of their stored vector pairs when they agree. When they do not, it calls a helper and subtracts the stored values from the helper's result.

name: negate_stored_accumulator_pair
description: Returns the negation of two 32-bit values stored at fixed offsets, packed into one 64-bit result.

name: store_scaled_fields_then_call
description: Stores a shifted and doubled 16-bit value into one structure and the high byte of another 16-bit field into a second structure. It then calls a helper.

name: store_byte_and_call
description: Stores the high byte of a 16-bit field from one structure at a negatively offset location in another, then calls a helper.

name: compute_clamped_bit_mask
description: Computes a one-bit mask by shifting one left by the difference between a register value and a field in another structure. A negative result is clamped to 127, and the byte is stored with a constant pair of 16-bit sentinel values.

name: project_and_store_transform_results
description: Calls a helper, then computes a scaled matrix product from its outputs and stores the components, a projected scale value, and a flag byte into a structure. A range check either stores a clamped scale or calls further helpers.

name: project_and_copy_vertex_data
description: Computes a scale from a magnitude count and stores a shifted value into a structure. It either copies a block of nine words or computes a matrix product before storing the results, and out-of-range values store sentinel constants and return early.

name: transform_vertex_matrix_block
description: Scales three input values by a magnitude count, forms row products against a 3 by 3 block, and stores the results and sentinel values into a structure. It calls helpers for range checks and for optional copies.

name: multiply_block_rows_then_flush
description: Computes three matrix-row products from two 3 by 3 blocks and stores them in the local frame, then calls two helpers. If a pending flag is set, it writes the constant 30 into a buffer, advances the buffer pointer, and clears the flag.

name: transform_block_rows_then_flush
description: Optionally calls a helper to select a second block, then computes nine matrix-row products from two 3 by 3 blocks into the local frame. It ends by clearing a sentinel word and flushing the pending flag.

name: select_block_and_transform
description: Sets two words of a structure to the minimum signed value, then either copies nine words from a block or computes nine matrix products, depending on flags. It finishes by flushing the pending flag.

name: flush_pending_marker_write
description: Calls a helper and, when a local flag is set, calls two more helpers. It then writes the constant 30 into a pending buffer if the global flag is set, advances the pointer, and clears the flag.

name: update_global_pointer_state
description: Calls helpers, then if a global flag is set, writes the constant 30 at the address held in a global pointer, advances that pointer by one word, and clears the flag.

name: flush_pending_marker_and_return
description: Runs helper calls and, when a global flag is set, writes the constant 30 into a buffer at a global pointer. It advances the pointer, clears the flag, and returns.

name: normalize_and_transform_vectors
description: Finds a shift count that brings the largest of three inputs within 16 bits, shifts the inputs accordingly, and then computes two sets of three matrix products from stored coefficients. The results are stored as 16-bit fixed-point values in a local context block.

name: compute_component_margin
description: Combines a scaled offset from the stack with two component magnitudes reduced by that offset, returning the first reduced magnitude or zero depending on comparisons against a third value.

name: clear_strided_words_table
description: Zeroes a column of 16-bit values at a fixed stride, handling ten rows per pass and then the remaining rows. The row count is taken from a shifted 16-bit field of an input structure.

name: clear_structured_memory
description: Zeroes five fixed-offset words in a local structure, then clears words in a table at a fixed stride. The row count is derived from a shifted input register.

name: fill_stack_with_constant
description: Writes one fixed 16-bit pattern into consecutive stack words, with the count taken from a field of a structure, halved and reduced by three. The loop runs while the count is non-negative.

name: build_projected_shape_entry
description: Clips a screen position against the 320 by 168 area and, when visible, writes a fixed header of constant words followed by projected corner coordinates into a display list. It assigns indices from a shared table to hold the entries.

name: emit_corner_projections_visible
description: Rejects positions whose horizontal or vertical extent leaves the 320 by 168 area, then writes a fixed header and projected corner coordinates into a display list. It reuses the same shape-index table as the other projection routines.

name: emit_projected_shape_unclipped
description: Rejects a degenerate extent, then writes a fixed header and projected corner coordinates into a display list. A flag-driven path sets the position from a stored offset instead.

name: write_projected_shape_corners
description: Writes a fixed header of constant words and a table-indexed value into a display list, then stores projected corner coordinates computed from two stacked offsets and a scaled divisor.

name: emit_shape_header_then_corners
description: Calls helpers, then writes a fixed header of constant words and table-indexed values into a display list. It finishes with projected corner coordinates computed from stacked offsets and a scaled divisor.

name: store_table_index_and_corners
description: Stores the low byte of a global counter into a byte table at a register index and writes a display-list word from the counter. It then records a second table index and stores projected corner coordinates from stacked offsets.

name: store_indexed_word_and_corners
description: Stores the low byte of a global counter into a byte table at a register index and writes a display-list word, without updating a list pointer. It then records a second table index and stores projected corner coordinates from stacked offsets.

name: append_display_entry_and_corners
description: Appends a four-byte record to a display list at its running offset, writes a table byte, and records a second table index. It then stores projected corner coordinates computed from stacked offsets.

name: append_display_entry_projected
description: Calls a helper, appends a four-byte record to a display list, and records a table index for the entry. It then stores projected corner coordinates computed from stacked offsets.

name: emit_sprite_display_record
description: Clips a position against the 320 by 168 area, then writes a display record with a type constant, coordinates, a mode value, and two table-indexed words. A second branch writes a different type constant with fewer fields when the mode falls outside a small range.

name: emit_flagged_sprite_record
description: Computes a flag-adjusted index, then writes a display record with a type constant, clipped coordinates, and table-indexed words. It uses the same clipped and unclipped branches as the other sprite emitters.

name: emit_sprite_record_with_indices
description: Writes a display record with a fixed type constant, two coordinates derived from a helper result and stacked inputs, and two table-indexed words.

name: emit_indexed_sprite_record
description: Writes a display record with a fixed type constant and coordinates, switching to a second constant and adjusted coordinates when a flag is set. It then stores two table-indexed words.

name: store_two_table_indices
description: Stores a counter-derived table index into a byte table and a display-list word, then records a second table index taken from a masked register value.

name: append_list_entry_and_index
description: Writes a byte into a table at a register index, appends a four-byte record to a display list, and stores the value in a word field. It then records a second table index derived from a masked register.

name: store_indexed_table_word
description: Writes a byte into a table at a register index and stores a counter-derived word into a structure field. The word is also taken from the counter when the index is valid.

name: append_list_record_word
description: Appends a four-byte record to a display list at its running offset, writes a table byte, and stores a word in a structure field.

name: emit_scaled_sprite_record
description: Derives a scale index from a stacked value and a shift count, then writes either a type-4F8 record with a zero index or a clipped display record with a table-indexed value. It stores table indices as it goes.

name: emit_scaled_sprite_record_alt
description: Derives a scale index from a register divisor and a shift count, then writes either a type-4F8 record or a clipped display record. It uses the same table-index steps as the other emitters.
